paragraphs: Pantonium sells on-demand transit software whose Macrotransit product uses artificial intelligence to adapt community transportation to rider demand through the day. The pages set that against microtransit and traditional fixed-route systems, and say a city is not divided into separate zones. Alongside the platform, the site lists transit planning, simulation and data analysis, Indigenous and rural community partnerships, and operational support and deployment expertise.

The platform is reached from any computer and any browser, and the page states that no hardware is required for setup or maintenance. A mobile application connects management and dispatchers to drivers through driver and GPS feedback, and collects location data that feeds dispatch and route planning. Listed features include assisted manual and automated dispatching, scheduling and driver work tracking, on-demand trip optimization, custom reports, live and historic vehicle locations, and trip imports from major brokers.

The home page says the company partners with communities, whether urban, rural, or Indigenous, to deliver public transportation solutions. The home page reports results from over a dozen transit services, among them a 3x increase in ridership and a 40% reduction in vehicle mileage.

quote.text: It sees the entire community, including city cores, rural edges, and underserved areas as one dynamic, unified service area.
